data.name: Serael
data.long_meaning: The name Serael is derived from the Hebrew word ‘saraph’, which means ‘a burning one’ or ‘a serpent’. In the Bible, seraphim are described as fiery, six-winged angels that surround God’s throne and cry out, ‘Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts’. So, the name Serael can be seen as representing the powerful and fiery presence of God.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the presence and power of God.
data.numerology_meaning: Represents the harmony of balance and love.

in_english.name: Serael
in_english.long_meaning: Serael is a name derived from Hebrew and Greek roots, meaning genuine, true, or sincere. It is associated with qualities of authenticity and integrity. In biblical context, it may refer to the seed of God's promise, symbolizing faithfulness and loyalty. In Christian tradition, Serael represents the true self, called to live in accordance with God's will. The name Serael is used in modern times to convey a sense of authenticity and commitment to one's values.

data.cultural_impact: The name Serael, with its roots in Hebrew, carries a rich cultural significance for Christians. Hebrew names have long been associated with the Jewish and Christian traditions, representing a deep connection to the ancient roots of the faith. The name Serael, specifically, can be seen as a reminder of the biblical imagery of fierce, celestial beings that surround God and declare His holiness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Serael represents the presence and power of God. The seraphim in the Bible are described as being in the very presence of God, and their fiery, six-winged appearance symbolizes the intensity and depth of God’s love and holiness. By adopting the name Serael, one can reflect on the profound nature of God and be reminded of His eternal and all-powerful presence. Additionally, the name can serve as a reminder to live a life that reflects the fiery intensity and passion of God.

historical_references.reference: The name Serael is derived from the Hebrew word 'serar' meaning 'to heal' or 'to raise up'. In the Old Testament, it is the name given to King Saul's son, whom the Prophet Samuel anointed as the next king of Israel. This event took place around 1050 BCE.

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament, Serael is mentioned as the name of the angel who appeared to Joseph in a dream and revealed that Mary's son would be called Jesus and that he would save his people from their sins. This event took place around 1 CE.
